subject: general
question: When parallel beam of light rays are incident on the convex mirror of focal length 1 m, reflected rays:

options.text: converge to a point at a distance 1 m from the convex surface
appear to diverge from a point at a distance 0.5 m behind the mirror
appear to diverge from a point at a distance 1 m behind the mirror
converge to a point at a distance 0.5 m from the convex surface

solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3: appear to diverge from a point at a distance 1 m behind the mirror**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A convex mirror is also known as a diverging mirror.
 
• When parallel rays of light strike a convex mirror, they appear to diverge from a single point behind the mirror.
 
• This point is called the focal point, and the distance from the mirror's surface to this point is called the focal length (f).
 
• For a convex mirror, the focal length is considered positive, and the focal point is virtual as the light rays do not actually converge there.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Convex Mirror:**

 
 
• A convex mirror is a spherical mirror in which the reflective surface bulges outwards.
 
• It is used in various applications like vehicle rearview mirrors and in surveillance.
 
 
 
• **Focal Length (f):**
 
 
• The focal length is the distance between the mirror's surface and the focal point.
 
• For a convex mirror, the focal length is positive and virtual.
 
 
 
• **Virtual Image:**
 
 
• A virtual image is formed when the reflected rays appear to diverge from a point behind the mirror.
 
• Virtual images cannot be projected on a screen as the light rays do not actually meet.
 
 
 
• **Diverging Mirror:**
 
 
• Convex mirrors are also known as diverging mirrors because they spread out light rays that are initially parallel when they reflect off the mirror.
 
 

The correct answer is **Option 2: Both the statements (I) and (II) are not related.**__.
